sources.text: Docinsight: Its Git history begins on 8 June 2026 with commits under omerfarooq223. Later commits and backend/app/services/radar_service.py plus backend/app/core/radar_scheduler.py show a monitoring feature that records a source baseline, hashes and compares later content, distinguishes unchanged or formatting-only updates, analyzes meaningful differences, and prepares email or Slack alerts. This extends the description from one-time research reports to continuing source surveillance; it does not prove that a scheduler ran continuously in production.

Workstream: AInsight; Professional work supported by the local repository: Contributed to an R&D decision-intelligence platform combining Productix R&D Co-Pilot and Docinsight Workspace. The FastAPI/Next.js system describes formulation and physical-trial workflows, scientific-document retrieval, evidence-backed reporting, and a colour-to-formulation feature with trial-feedback correction. The local README combines current and planned features, so this entry describes repository scope rather than claiming every workflow was production-tested.

sources.section: 3.5 Evidence-backed chronology and useful cross-project insights
sources.text: The Docinsight-to-AInsight relationship is stronger than a similar name. Their local repositories have the same root commit; AInsight's later history adds R&D agent, supplier, trial, and colour workflows. A RAG answer may say that AInsight grew from a shared Docinsight code lineage, but should not collapse their names into one product or assume every Docinsight feature shipped in AInsight.

AI-Resume-Screening-Bias-Detection (https://github.com/Sobanshahid10/AI-Resume-Screening-Bias-Detection) — AI resume screening with bias detection, fairness auditing, and human review. Soban's project post (https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7490647797101400066/) calls the jointly built product ClarityHire and describes FastAPI, Celery, SQLAlchemy, React/Vite, Sentence Transformers, Fairlearn, Groq, Redis Pub/Sub, server-sent events, and a four-stage screening pipeline. It reports deployment using Vercel, Render, Supabase, and Redis Cloud, with human review of scored candidates. The CV additionally reports PII anonymization, hybrid semantic/feature scoring, explainable candidate ranking, synthetic demographic fairness audits, asynchronous processing, SQL persistence, and PDF/HTML/CSV reports. It says protected attributes are not used for scoring; implementation and audit results should be checked against the repository before treating that as verified behavior.

OS Pilot (https://github.com/omerfarooq223/ospilot-agent) — Local-first developer-workspace recovery agent and Kaggle capstone project. Its README describes project-aware scanning, manifest-backed rebuildability scoring, recovery recipes, comparison of Conservative/Balanced/Deep Review cleanup plans, and human approval before moving selected files to reversible quarantine. It uses React/Vite/Tauri, FastAPI, SQLite, restricted tools, and a multi-agent planning pipeline. The README identifies Umar as team lead and Soban, Haseeb, and Abdullah as project partners; it does not establish which individual implemented each component.
